summary: Proposes a new Routing Policy Specification Language attribute so a network can advertise an IP address that is reachable and can be used for diagnostic tests like pings. This helps debug intermittent reachability for new connectivity. It is a Proposed Standard.

plainLanguage.summary: Leave a spare doorbell for visitors to press to check your house is reachable.

questions: how to advertise a diagnostic address
what is the rpsl pingable attribute
how to advertise a ping test address
subtitle: A routing registry attribute that lets a network publish an address others may ping to test reachability.

tldr.problem: New IP connectivity often has intermittent reachability, and operators lack a standard way to learn which host in a remote network is meant to be used for diagnostic tests.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds optional pingable and ping-hdl attributes to the RPSL route and route6 objects, giving a test address inside the route's range and a contact handle.
tldr.outcome: Testers can find an address meant for pings and Path MTU discovery, and are asked to send no more than ten probes in a five-minute window unless they have arranged otherwise.

facts.label: Rate limit
facts.value: No more than ten probes in five minutes

today: RFC 5943 is a Proposed Standard. It has not been obsoleted or updated according to the metadata for this RFC.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
New IP connectivity typically results in intermittent reachability for reasons outside this document's scope. To help debug such problems, the RFC creates a new attribute for the Routing Policy Specification Language (RPSL) that lets a network advertise an IP address that is reachable and can be a target for diagnostic tests such as pings.

The goal is to give operators a way to advertise selected hosts that can be test targets for common issues such as reachability and Path MTU discovery.
sections.plainLanguage: When a new connection acts up, it helps to have an agreed address to test against.

sections.title: The pingable Attribute
sections.content:
Operators MAY advertise a diagnostic address through RPSL. The pingable attribute is a member of the route and route6 objects. It holds an IPv6 or IPv4 address and is optional and multi-valued. The companion ping-hdl attribute holds a NIC handle, and is also optional and multi-valued.

The address MUST fall within the address range of the route or route6 object that contains the attribute. The ping-hdl links to contact information for an entity able to answer questions about the address.
sections.plainLanguage: The test address has to be one that belongs to the network that lists it, and a contact is named in case of questions.

sections.title: Using the Attribute
sections.content: One or more pingable attributes tell other operators that the target network provides the address(es) for external diagnostic testing. Tests using the address SHOULD be rate limited to no more than ten probes in a five-minute window unless prior arrangements are made with the maintainer of the attribute.
sections.plainLanguage: You may knock on the test door, but not over and over. A few knocks every few minutes is polite.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
RPSL-based routing registries need a significant level of security, and authentication in RPSL is key given the possible abuse of the attribute. Publishing the attribute only explicitly signals an ICMP Echo Request/Echo Response service on that address, though the operator MAY run other services there that could be affected by the publicity.

There is no guarantee that outsiders will rate limit, so operators are encouraged to deploy their own rate limiting to reduce denial-of-service risk, and to filter services, protocols and ports not intended for external users.
sections.plainLanguage: Not everyone will knock politely, so the owner should limit visitors and lock the doors that are not meant for guests.

data.title: route6 object with pingable
data.code:
route6: 2001:DB8::/32
origin: AS64500
pingable: 2001:DB8::DEAD:BEEF
ping-hdl: OPS4-RIPE
